scope: Oregon/Tillamook design-basis review for a proposed deployable two-half pedestrian overpass; applicability remains project-specific.

sources.title: Highway Design Manual, Part 300: Cross Section Elements
sources.supported_use: Pedestrian-overpass clearance of 17 ft 4 in, excluding future overlays; route and jurisdiction distinctions.
sources.applicability_limit: Responsible road/bridge authority must establish classification and applicable site criteria.

sources.title: Bridge Design Manual, Section 2
sources.supported_use: Clearance coordination, future overlays and separate construction-state criteria.
sources.applicability_limit: Generic high-route table says 17.25 ft, distinct from HDM pedestrian 17 ft 4 in; discrepancy retained, not resolved by this study.

sources.title: Bridge Design Manual, Section 1.17: Seismic and Tsunami Design
sources.supported_use: Ordinary-bridge seismic provisions for new pedestrian bridges over vehicular roads; project-specific seismic criteria for non-conventional structures.
sources.applicability_limit: Mobile, temporary and diversion classifications are not determined here.

sources.title: Temporary Pedestrian Accessible Routes Overview
sources.supported_use: Work-zone accessible-route continuity, slopes, widths and landing dimensions.
sources.applicability_limit: The specified highway/work-zone scope does not itself determine new public-overpass access compliance.

sources.title: Public Right-of-Way Accessibility Guidelines, Chapter 2
sources.supported_use: Temporary facilities, pedestrian overpasses, compliant approaches and limited platform-lift exception.
sources.applicability_limit: Do not assert universal adoption; determine governing adopted standards for the project.

sources.title: Engineering for Accessibility
sources.supported_use: Current ODOT explanation of PROWAG adoption for transit and continuing DOJ review; current discipline design manuals.
sources.applicability_limit: Adoption status and facility scope must be checked at project design acceptance.

sources.title: Implementing Uniform Traffic Control Devices
sources.supported_use: Oregon adoption of MUTCD 11th Edition Revision 1, June 2026 supplement and January 2026 handbook.
sources.applicability_limit: A source reference does not constitute a site-specific traffic plan or closure authorization.

sources.title: Oregon Temporary Traffic Control Handbook
sources.supported_use: Accommodation of all road users and accessible alternatives in short-duration work zones.
sources.applicability_limit: Handbook scope is work zones continuously in place for three days or less; project traffic control still needs design.

sources.publisher: David Evans and Associates for ODOT and Tillamook County
sources.title: Technical Memorandum 2: Plan and Policy Review Summary
sources.supported_use: City TSP 2019 and street-level crossing recommendations at 7th, 9th and 11th Streets.
sources.applicability_limit: Summarizes the 2018 crossing study; not an overpass recommendation or evidence of current construction status.

sources.title: Tillamook County Transportation System Plan update
sources.supported_use: Rural/unincorporated county scope and planned spring 2027 adoption.
sources.applicability_limit: Draft update; distinct from the City's 2019 plan.

sources.title: Northwest Oregon Pedestrian Safety Upgrades
sources.supported_use: Planned US 101 pedestrian improvements at MP64.4 and MP124.4; construction scheduled 2027.
sources.applicability_limit: No cross-street assignment or project geometry inferred from milepost text.

sources.title: National Flood Hazard Layer: Flood Hazard Zones
sources.supported_use: Effective flood-zone/subtype attributes and available elevation/datum fields.
sources.applicability_limit: Coverage and source citations require review; does not determine local permit consequences or site suitability.

sources.title: National Flood Hazard Layer
sources.supported_use: NFHL compiles effective FIRMs and map revisions and can provide regulatory flood information.
sources.applicability_limit: Not a replacement for reviewing the actual effective records for a site.
